newsitem.title: USA: Soros fund officials questioned on Eurotunnel shrs.
newsitem.headline: Soros fund officials questioned on Eurotunnel shrs.

text.p: French authorities have questioned officials of the multibillion-dollar fund led by investor and philanthropist George Soros in an investigation into possible insider trading of Eurotunnel SA shares, a fund spokesman said Thursday.
Shawn Pattison told Reuters that senior executives of Soros Fund Management met with French investigators two days ago in New York.

"Soros Fund Management has provided whatever assistance has been asked from these authorities," Pattison said. "Our trading in the Eurotunnel has been completely appropriate and legal in all respects."

He confirmed British newspaper reports that France's Police de la Brigade Financiere were investigating banks and brokers who might have traded in Eurotunnel shares they did not own before a 1994 rights issue.
The bankers and brokers allegedly made huge profits after the shares dropped sharply following the issue.

"To the best of our knowledge, the French authorities have been investigating trading in Eurotunnel shares for quite some time," Pattison said. "This has included questioning a wide range of New York-based financial institutions."
He said he did not know how much the fund had invested in the shares.
Soros Management Fund has about $18 billion in assets.
